requirement:
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
rationale:
I found no test-adequacy gap in the supplied tests. The tests in `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/selector.rs` and `crates/trust-but-verify/src/outline/tests.rs` cover each obligation of `requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`. I did not request implementation source.

- **`/`-separated path and empty selector selects the root.**
  - `parses_named_anonymous_and_ordinal_segments` asserts that `parse_selector("")` is empty. It also parses a multi-segment path.
  - It rejects malformed selectors such as `a//b`, `fn`, `fn[run`, `[run]`, `fn[run]x` and `fn[run]#0`.
  - `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` asserts `outline.resolve("") == 0`. It also resolves nested paths such as `mod[local]/fn[run]` and `fn[outer]/fn[inner]`.
- **Named segment `kind[name]`.** Both `rust_selectors_follow_syntactic_ancestry` and `selectors_name_syntactic_ancestry_and_duplicates` assert many exact generated selectors, and the first also round-trips each through `resolve`. `Segment::base` and `Segment` display are asserted in the parse test.
- **Anonymous segment `kind@hash` with the first 12 hex digits of the identity hash.**
  - `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes` asserts the `use@` prefix and a length of 12 hex digits.
  - It shows that a selector survives unrelated insertions and stops resolving when the node's own content changes.
  - `anonymous_container_selectors_use_identity_hashes_and_survive_descendant_edits` asserts the selector equals `pair[items]/item@{identity_hash[..12]}`. It also checks that it differs from the structural hash and survives descendant edits.
  - The hash computation itself is a cited requirement and is not reassessed here.
- **`#N` disambiguation, one-based and in source order.**
  - `fn[repeated]#1` and `#2` are asserted in the Rust tests. Identical `use` statements get `#1` and `#2` in `anonymous_selectors_use_identity_hashes`.
  - `duplicate_names_are_numbered_in_source_order_without_line_numbers` asserts the byte start of `#1` and the line starts. It also shows that swapping the declarations swaps the ordinals.
  - The ambiguous selector `fn[repeated]` is rejected by `resolve`.
- **`line` exception.** `plain_text_lines_are_interchangeable_anonymous_nodes` has identical lines `alpha` twice. It asserts both get the same `line@…` selector with no `#N`, and that the selector resolves.
- **Percent-encoding of `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`, `@` and whitespace as UTF-8 bytes.**
  - `names_round_trip_through_percent_encoding` asserts the exact encoding, including tab, NBSP and ideographic space as multi-byte sequences.
  - It asserts decoding round-trips and that raw `/`, `%zz` and a raw space are rejected.
  - `impl[%5Bu8;%204%5D]/fn[edge]` is asserted in the outline tests, and the parse test decodes `Trait%3CT%3E`.
- **No line numbers in selectors.** `duplicate_names_are_numbered_in_source_order_without_line_numbers` prepends blank lines and asserts that the selectors and the structural hash are unchanged while `line_start` moves from 1 to 4.

There are no marking gaps: every relevant test carries a `{test}` reference to the subject.

text: :::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} structural_hash
A node's structural hash MUST be the SHA-256 digest of an unambiguous encoding of
its outline-relevant structure, including siblings its profile attaches to it:
the kinds of its named grammar nodes and, in source order, its text pieces. A
text piece MUST be the text of a leaf token, or text inside a node that no child
token covers. Each text piece MUST be hashed as its ordered list of words, where
words are separated by whitespace, the whitespace itself, including leading and
trailing whitespace, is never hashed, and each word is encoded separately, so
`ab cd` and `abcd` differ. The same rule MUST apply in every language. Comments
MUST be excluded, except comment kinds the profile includes; the Rust profile MUST include doc comments. For an included comment, only its text and its
profile's comment group MUST be hashed, not its delimiter tokens such as `//`,
`///`, `//!`, `/*`, `*/`, or a leading `*`; the Rust profile's groups are inner
and outer doc comments. The words of consecutive included comments of one group
MUST be hashed as one ordered list, so reflowing them across more or fewer lines
or comments does not change the hash, while moving text between groups does. A `line`
node's hash MUST be computed by the same word rule over the line's text. A node's
identity hash MUST be computed the same way but MUST also exclude its outline
descendants and their attached siblings, so editing a descendant does not change
its ancestors' selectors.
